meta.subtitle: Fiber and 5G are growing and the cash yield is high, but the EchoStar leverage step-up and a satellite scare cap the multiple

analystSentiment.commentary:
AT&T's second quarter of 2026 delivered what the investment-led plan promised. Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew {+ +5.1% +} year over year to $23.5 billion, segment operating income rose {+ +20.3% +}, and the company added 432,000 postpaid phones and 646,000 internet connections while postpaid phone churn held at 0.86%. Consolidated revenue of $31.6B grew a slower 2.3% because the Legacy segment, which the company is powering down, shrank {- -25.9% -}. Free cash flow of $4.7 billion came in above the company's own $4 billion-$4.5 billion range for the quarter, and management reiterated $18 billion+ for the year.

The shares trade at a 9.7% trailing free-cash-flow yield, with a forward multiple and a dividend yield to match, and the buyback pace for 2026 was lifted to approximately $10 billion. Even so, three things keep us at HOLD. EchoStar raises leverage first and lowers it later, on a timetable management measures in years, and that window limits how much of the $45 billion+ capital-return plan can be pulled forward. Convergence is diluting fiber ARPU, so subscriber growth is buying revenue growth at a lower price per line. And satellite competition now sits between the shares and a re-rating; the risk section carries the evidence and the metric that would settle it.

Our probability-weighted value sits modestly above the current price of $26.53, and the Street's consensus target sits exactly at the current price, which says the same. The dividend and the buyback carry the return until the leverage path after EchoStar is visible. We would turn more constructive on evidence that Advanced Connectivity EBITDA growth holds at the 6%+ guided for 2026 while net leverage begins to fall.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
AT&T Inc. is a Dallas-based holding company whose subsidiaries provide wireless and wireline connectivity in the United States and wireless service in Mexico. Effective with its Q1 2026 reporting, the company realigned its segments into Advanced Connectivity (domestic 5G and fiber-based wireless, internet and other connectivity services for consumer and business customers), Legacy (domestic voice and data services over the copper-based network it plans to stop operating across the large majority of its footprint by the end of 2029), and Latin America (wireless service and equipment in Mexico). The United States produced 95.7% of FY25 revenue and Mexico 3.5%.

FY25 revenue was $125.6B. The vendor's product mix, which the segment chart follows, uses six labels that do not map to the company's three reporting segments; the moat section reconciles each label to the 10-Q. In the second quarter of 2026 the Advanced Connectivity segment produced $28,615 million of the $31,558 million of consolidated operating revenues, Legacy $1,632 million and Latin America $1,224 million.

At June 30, 2026 the wireless base stood at 109,800 thousand retail subscribers (74,921 thousand postpaid phones) and the internet base at 15,479 thousand connections, of which 12,868 thousand were fiber and 2,611 thousand fixed wireless. Fiber reached 38.6 million consumer and business locations at the end of the quarter. On February 2, 2026 the company closed its acquisition of substantially all of Lumen's Mass Markets fiber business; the acquired network assets sit in a subsidiary, Forged Fiber, in which the company intends to sell a controlling interest to an equity partner and which it therefore reports as discontinued operations. A planned purchase of spectrum licenses from EchoStar was expected to close by the end of July 2026.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
AT&T is two businesses moving in opposite directions. Advanced Connectivity, which management told the call contributes over 90% of service revenue and nearly all of adjusted EBITDA, grew service revenue {+ +5.1% +} in the second quarter with segment EBITDA up {+ +8.0% +} and an operating margin of 25.7%, up from 22.2% a year earlier. Legacy revenue fell {- -25.9% -}, and management guides Legacy EBITDA to turn negative after 2027 until the copper network's direct costs are gone. The consolidated result is low-single-digit revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA growth guided at 3% to 4% for 2026 and adjusted EPS guided at $2.25 to $2.35.

At 11.3x NTM earnings the market already prices the mix shift as slow, and the cash yield does the rest of the work. We think the cash return is secure: free cash flow of $18 billion+ guided for 2026 funds the $1.11 annualized dividend and the approximately $10 billion of 2026 buybacks that management says together absorb essentially 100% of the free-cash-flow outlook. What it does not fund is deleveraging, and the EchoStar spectrum purchase lifts net leverage to a post-close peak before it comes back down. We rate the shares HOLD: the yield pays investors to wait, but a re-rating needs the leverage peak behind it and proof that satellite entrants do not raise churn.

catalysts: Closing of the EchoStar spectrum license purchase, which management expected by the end of July 2026, fixes the leverage peak; the sooner the ratio turns back toward target, the sooner buybacks beyond the plan become possible.

Third-quarter free cash flow guided as relatively stable year over year, followed by a fourth quarter management expects to grow as last year's legal settlements and pension contribution do not recur.

Fiber expansion of 8 million new locations this year, including over 4 million acquired from Lumen, with converged gross adds in the acquired territories rising from February to June; the moat section carries the footprint targets.

FCC discontinuance approvals, now covering over 30% of wire centers effective by late 2026 and about 60% of California wire centers, gate the Legacy exit and the copper cost structure behind it; the risk section carries what stranded cost looks like if approvals slow.
Sale of a controlling interest in Forged Fiber to an equity partner, which would bring co-investment into the acquired Lumen network build and settle how the asset is carried.
risks: Satellite competition: SpaceX headlines hit AT&T's shares in early July 2026; the risk section carries the mechanism and the churn figure to watch.
Fiber ARPU fell 1.3% year over year; the risk section carries the cause and what would make it worse.
Interest expense rose in the quarter, and the post-close leverage peak adds to it; trailing interest coverage is 3.6x.
Business transitional and other revenue fell 16.6% and prepaid phone subscribers fell 3.4%; the shrinking lines still sit inside Advanced Connectivity, and the moat section carries the drivers.
Benefit-plan costs flow through reported earnings under the accounting election described in the February 2026 10-K; the risk section carries the drivers.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue of $125.6B grew {+ +2.7% +} after three flat-to-down years (FY22 {- -9.9% -}, FY23 +1.4%, FY24 -0.1%). Operating margin has been steady where revenue has not: 20.2% in FY23, 19.8% in FY24 and 19.9% in FY25, which is also why we read the vendor table's gross margin swing from 43.7% in FY23 to 59.6% in FY25 as a classification change rather than an operating one. The FY22 loss (operating margin of -3.8%, diluted EPS of -$1.13) reflects charges that year that the pack does not itemize. FY25 net income was $21.9B and diluted EPS $3.04; the valuation section explains why we value the shares on forward rather than trailing earnings.

The second quarter of 2026 is cleaner. Consolidated operating revenues rose 2.3% to $31,558 million, with service revenue growth ahead of equipment growth of 0.5%; operating income rose 8.3% to $7,038 million as depreciation fell 5.4% on fully depreciated legacy assets. Operating income margin improved to 22.3% from 21.1%, and for the six months to 21.7% from a year earlier. Income from continuing operations of $5,038 million grew more slowly because interest expense rose to $1,883 million from $1,655 million on higher debt balances and rates, and equity income from affiliates fell away after the DIRECTV stake sale on July 2, 2025. The effective tax rate fell to 13.5% on resolved IRS examinations, which helped diluted EPS from continuing operations reach $0.66; adjusted EPS of $0.65 compares with $0.54 a year earlier per the release. Operations and support expense carried an asset abandonment charge tied to the reprioritized spectrum strategy, higher advertising, bad debt from subscriber growth and the Lumen customer costs, offset by transformation savings, lower content fees and tower gains.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
The FY25 vendor table shows total debt of $174.0B and net debt of $155.8B at December 31, 2025, while the release reports total debt of $144.0 billion and net debt of $126.4 billion at June 30, 2026; the two sets are six months apart and not comparable as stated, and we use the release figures because they match the reporting period and are the ones management guides to. The same applies to the ratio: the vendor's trailing net debt to EBITDA of 2.7x rests on the FY25 balance, while management's 2.68 times at quarter end, essentially flat with the March quarter, rests on the release's June figure, and the report uses management's. Management expects the ratio to rise to the 3.2 times range when the EchoStar spectrum purchase closes and to return to the two and a half times range within approximately three years; that path, not the current level, is the constraint on capital returns, and every later reference in this report to the leverage peak or the deleveraging window means this sequence.

Cash rose to $18.2B at FY25 from $3.3B at FY24, which lifted the current ratio to 0.91 from 0.66; the trailing figure is 0.97, and trailing interest coverage is 3.6x. Management said on the call that the company is well-positioned to fund the EchoStar transaction. Total equity of $128.5B at FY25 sits well below the $183.9B of FY21 per the table; the step down came in FY22, the same year the table shows an operating loss, and equity has rebuilt slowly since. The February 2026 10-K flags that rating downgrades would raise borrowing costs and could require collateral posting under derivative agreements, which matters more as debt rises to fund spectrum.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow of $40.3B in FY25 funded capital expenditure of $20.8B, leaving free cash flow of $19.4B, a 15.5% margin, below the FY21 level of $25.4B; the FY22 trough was $12.4B, and FY23 and FY24 came in at $20.5B and $18.5B. Shareholder returns stepped up: repurchases of $6.6B in FY25, up from $0.2B in FY24 per the vendor table, on top of $8.2B of dividends.

The second quarter of 2026 continued the pattern. Cash from operating activities from continuing operations was $10.8 billion, up from $9.8 billion, on lower cash taxes and working-capital timing, net of a voluntary $100 million pension contribution. Capital expenditures were $5.7 billion, and capital investment, which adds vendor-financing payments of $0.4 billion, was $6.1 billion, up from $5.1 billion as fiber deployment accelerated. Free cash flow of $4.7 billion exceeded the $4 billion-$4.5 billion range management had set for the quarter. The company returned $4.1 billion, including approximately $2.2 billion of repurchases, and said it was on pace for nearly $1 billion of buybacks in July.

For the full year management holds free cash flow at $18 billion+ on capital investment of $23 billion to $24 billion, with third-quarter free cash flow expected to be relatively stable year over year and the fourth quarter to grow. Planned repurchases of approximately $10 billion plus the dividend consume the whole free-cash-flow outlook on management's own arithmetic, so debt reduction after EchoStar depends on EBITDA growth rather than retained cash.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $26.53 the shares trade at 8.8x trailing earnings, 11.3x NTM earnings, ~10.4x FY27E EPS of $2.56, 6.1x trailing EV/EBITDA and 1.4x sales, with a 9.7% trailing free-cash-flow yield and a 4.18% dividend yield. The trailing P/E flatters: FY25 diluted EPS of $3.04 sits well above the FY26E consensus of $2.34, so the forward multiples are the ones to use. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source, so we anchor on the company's own guidance instead: adjusted EPS of $2.25 to $2.35 for 2026 with a double-digit three-year CAGR through 2028, and free cash flow of $18 billion+ for 2026 guided to rise in each of 2027 and 2028.

The Street sees fair value at the price: 62 analysts, Buy 26, Hold 30, Sell 6, with a consensus target equal to the current price and a median of $27.50 inside a $20.00–$30.00 range. The shares sit in the upper half of their 52-week range of $19.89–$29.79 after the early-July sell-off. The free-cash-flow yield is the bull's core argument for a business guiding free cash flow up each year through 2028; the bear's is that the yield is spoken for by dividends and buybacks while net leverage rises after EchoStar, and that satellite competition can compress telecom multiples on headlines alone.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Advanced Connectivity service revenue keeps growing at the 5%+ guided for 2026 and segment EBITDA at 6%+, the $4 billion cost program lands by the end of 2028, and free cash flow reaches the $21 billion+ guided for 2028; with the EchoStar leverage peak behind it and no visible satellite share loss, the market pays a premium to today's NTM multiple for a business whose Legacy drag is ending.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Guidance is met as issued: adjusted EPS lands inside $2.25 to $2.35 for 2026 and consensus FY27E EPS of $2.56 holds, the dividend of $1.11 is maintained and approximately $10 billion of buybacks are completed this year; the shares keep roughly the current 11.3x NTM multiple applied to FY27E earnings, with the dividend making up most of the total return.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Satellite entrants and promotional intensity lift postpaid phone churn from 0.86% and slow wireless service revenue growth below the 3.3% of the second quarter; fiber ARPU keeps sliding, the leverage ratio sits near its post-close peak for longer, buybacks are cut to protect the dividend, and the multiple compresses toward the low end of the Street's $20.00–$30.00 target range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We put half the weight on the Base case at $29 and split the rest evenly between a Bull case at $33 and a Bear case at $21. The Base case is management's own plan discounted at the current multiple: it requires no re-rating, and its return comes from earnings growth toward FY27E plus the dividend. The Bull case needs the two things the market is withholding, a lower leverage peak after EchoStar and evidence that satellite competition is not a churn event; we give it a one-in-four chance because the second quarter's net adds and margin gains are consistent with it, but a single quarter does not establish it. The Bear case carries the same weight because the satellite risk set out in the risk section is already moving the shares, and because a pull-forward of buybacks to approximately $10 billion in 2026 leaves less cushion if free cash flow disappoints.

The probability-weighted value lands above the current price by a mid-single-digit percentage, inside the HOLD envelope, and our $25–$31 target range brackets the Base case. A move toward BUY would follow leverage turning down from its post-EchoStar peak with Advanced Connectivity EBITDA growth intact; a move toward SELL would follow postpaid phone churn rising or fiber net adds slowing while the leverage ratio is still elevated.

segments.name: Wireless Service
segments.body: The vendor's Wireless Service label corresponds to the wireless service line inside the 10-Q's Advanced Connectivity segment. Second-quarter 2026 wireless service revenue grew 3.3% year over year to $17,413 million on subscriber growth in underpenetrated categories, converged accounts and pricing actions, partially offset by promotional discounts on new subscribers. The company added 432,000 postpaid phones in the quarter with postpaid phone churn of 0.86%, down from 0.87% a year earlier. This is the cash engine, and its growth rate is the number the satellite debate is really about.

segments.name: Other Capitalized Property Plant and Equipment
segments.body: The vendor's Other Capitalized Property Plant and Equipment label maps to no 10-Q revenue line, and the vendor does not say what it contains. On size, the desk's own inference is that it is equipment revenue, the handsets and devices sold alongside service, which the 10-Q reports at $5,581 million for the second quarter and $11,609 million for the six months, higher on wireless device sales volumes; the mapping is ours, not the vendor's. Equipment revenue carries little margin and moves with promotional activity, so we set it aside when judging the moat.

segments.name: Business Service
segments.body: The vendor's Business Service label spans two 10-Q lines: business fiber and advanced connectivity, which grew 10.0% in the second quarter to $1,946 million on fiber and fixed wireless, and business transitional and other, which fell {- -16.6% -} to $1,042 million on lower VPN and wholesale demand that management expects to continue. Our read is that the combined line's growth is a mix outcome: it accelerates only as the shrinking line becomes small enough to stop offsetting the growing one, and one quarter of combined growth is not yet evidence that the corner has been turned. Business is a stabilizer for the moat rather than a source of it.

segments.name: Legacy Voice and Data
segments.body: The vendor's Legacy Voice and Data label is closest to the 10-Q's Legacy segment, domestic voice and data over the copper-based network. Second-quarter Legacy revenues fell {- -25.9% -} to $1,632 million and EBITDA fell {- -45.5% -} to $523 million, with the margin down to 32.0% from 43.6% as revenue left faster than direct cost. Guidance has Legacy service revenue declining 20%+ in 2026 and immaterial by the end of 2029, with Legacy EBITDA negative after 2027 until the direct costs of the copper network are substantially eliminated; FCC approvals now cover over 30% of wire centers for discontinuance effective by late 2026. Legacy is a cost to be removed, not a franchise.

segments.name: IP Broadband
segments.body: The vendor's IP Broadband label is a fraction of what the 10-Q reports as advanced home internet, which grew {+ +27.3% +} in the second quarter to $2,926 million on fiber revenues up 21.4% (including the acquired Lumen customers) and AT&T Internet Air revenue more than doubling. Internet net adds were 646,000, of which 367,000 were fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless. The vendor's label understates this line; the 10-Q's version is the one that matters, and its growth rate is the moat's forward edge.

segments.name: Other Service
segments.body: The vendor's Other Service label matches the 10-Q's other service line, which reflects consumer VoIP and fell 7.9% in the second quarter to $151 million as the customer count keeps declining. It is immaterial to the thesis.

geoMix.region: Region of Latin America and Caribbean excluding Brazil

moatFactors.name: Fiber footprint and convergence
moatFactors.body: Fiber passes 38.6 million locations with a target of over 40 million by the end of 2026 and more than 60 million by the end of 2030, and internet connections grew 29.5% year over year to 15,479 thousand with fiber connections up 22.8%. The convergence rate, the share of advanced home internet households that also take AT&T postpaid wireless, was 42.5%, and management says converged customers show lower churn, higher lifetime value and higher brand affinity. The counter sits in the same disclosure: the rate reached 45% excluding the acquired Lumen footprint, so the headline is diluted by an under-penetrated acquired base, and the acquired customers add less near term than their count suggests.

moatFactors.name: Spectrum and network scale
moatFactors.body: Management told the call that the company already has an advantaged low-band position and that what it called 'the 600' will make that advantage more substantial; the pack does not say what the 600 is, so we do not tie it to the EchoStar licenses. The scale behind the position is visible in the base: retail wireless subscribers stood at 109,800 thousand at June 30, 2026 with postpaid phones up 2.1% to 74,921 thousand, and postpaid phone churn edged lower year over year, so scale is holding customers without a churn cost. The counter is that spectrum is bought rather than built, and the EchoStar purchase is what creates the post-close leverage peak.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs from bundling
moatFactors.body: Build-A-Plan, expanded on June 30, 2026 to let customers add AT&T Fiber or AT&T Internet Air to a customizable wireless plan, is designed to raise the share of two-product households. The cost of that design is price: converged accounts get discounted pricing, and the ARPU dilution from convergence described in the risk section is the bill for it. Switching costs exist, but they are being purchased with discounts.

moatFactors.name: Operating leverage and cost position
moatFactors.body: Advanced Connectivity operating income rose {+ +20.3% +} to $7,345 million in the second quarter on segment revenue up 4.1%, taking the segment operating margin to 25.7% from 22.2% and the EBITDA margin to 42.0% from 40.5%. Depreciation fell as legacy assets reached full depreciation, transformation initiatives are on pace for $4 billion of annual savings by the end of 2028, and the copper exit is meant to remove the direct costs that keep Legacy EBITDA positive today. Operations and support expense still rose in the quarter on advertising, bad debt and Lumen customer costs, so the consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin of 39.1% is the reference point to watch.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is narrow because the evidence for pricing power is thin: the 10-Q's own account of wireless service growth, quoted under Wireless Service above, credits pricing actions net of promotional discounts and calls churn management critical to margins, which is the language of a market where share is bought. Satellite is the second reason: a moat that the market can re-price on a headline, as the risk section describes, is not a wide one. What is durable is the fiber footprint: locations passed cannot be replicated quickly, the company is adding 8 million new locations this year with Lumen's acquired footprint among them, and management expects 2026 to exceed every prior year for fiber expansion. Latin America, the Mexico wireless business at 3.5% of FY25 revenue, grew revenue 16.1% in the quarter on foreign exchange and postpaid growth but adds nothing to the moat. Our view is that the moat widens if the convergence rate keeps rising and narrows if satellite entrants reset wireless pricing; the legacy exit removes a drag on returns rather than adding protection.

points: Advanced Connectivity is guided to mid-single-digit service revenue growth annually through 2028, including 5%+ in 2026, with segment EBITDA growth in the mid-to-high-single-digit range and 6%+ in 2026; the second quarter's {+ +5.1% +} service revenue growth accelerated by 150 basis points from the March quarter.

Advanced home internet is the growth line: revenue rose {+ +27.3% +} in the quarter on 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless net adds, and AT&T Internet Air connections nearly doubled to 1,951 thousand; management expects revenue growth to continue as the fiber footprint expands toward over 40 million locations by year end.

Wireless growth is coming from accounts rather than lines: 147,000 consumer postpaid wireless accounts were added in the quarter, which management said it had not matched in more than three years, and postpaid phone ARPU grew year over year while churn fell; pricing actions that took effect during the quarter support second-half service revenue.

Business is turning: Business Advanced Connectivity service revenues grew 1.8% in the quarter on wireless, fiber and fixed wireless, and management expects them to grow at a low single-digit CAGR through 2028; Business transitional and other, down {- -16.6% -} on VPN and wholesale, will keep subtracting.

Consolidated growth stays low-single-digit because Legacy service revenue is guided down 20%+ in 2026; the arithmetic improves as Legacy shrinks toward immaterial by the end of 2029, which is why adjusted EBITDA growth is guided to improve from 3% to 4% in 2026 and to accelerate by 2028.

Consensus already assumes this path: FY26E revenue of ~$129.2B and FY27E of $131.9B, with EPS of $2.34 and $2.56; the growth case is about whether the mix shift shows up in the multiple, not in the estimates.

management.leadership: John T. Stankey serves as both Chairman and CEO, as the release identifies him, so the board's leadership and its oversight of management sit with the same person. The March 2026 proxy states that the Corporate Governance Guidelines require a substantial majority of the Board to be independent, that the Board affirmatively determined the directors it names to be independent, and that every member of the Audit, Governance and Policy, and Human Resources Committees is independent; the excerpt gives no board size, so the ratio cannot be checked here. Operationally the team has delivered the plan it set out in early 2026: the second quarter's free cash flow ran ahead of the company's own range, all consolidated full-year and multi-year guidance was reiterated, and the segment realignment gives outside investors a clean view of the copper exit. Our reservation is stylistic. The call's framing of agentic AI traffic growth (up to 450% more traffic per task, 9X enterprise and 7X consumer traffic growth by 2035) is industry research cited by management rather than a company forecast, and the shares should not be valued on it.
management.capitalAllocation: The framework is explicit: capital investment of $23 billion to $24 billion a year through 2028, a dividend held at $1.11 per share annualized, approximately $24 billion of repurchases over 2026–2028 with approximately $10 billion in 2026 (raised from a prior $8 billion target and pulled forward from later years), and $45 billion+ of total returns over the three years. Second-quarter returns were $4.1 billion including approximately $2.2 billion of buybacks, and FY25 repurchases of $6.6B were a step up from the prior year on the vendor table. Two judgments sit inside this. One is the EchoStar spectrum purchase, which sets the leverage peak; buying spectrum while accelerating buybacks means the balance sheet, not the equity, absorbs the timing. The other is the Lumen fiber purchase, structured so that a controlling interest in the network assets is to be sold to an equity partner; if that sale closes on acceptable terms it recycles capital, and if it does not, the assets return to continuing operations with their build cost.
management.governance: The March 2026 proxy shows compensation set by a Human Resources Committee composed entirely of independent directors and a 2025 say-on-pay vote of 90.7% support. The 2025 short-term plan paid a 112% weighted average: compensation-adjusted operating income, at a 60% weight, attained 104% and paid 118%; free cash flow, at a 20% weight, attained 100% and paid 101%; and the strategic component, at the same weight, has no stated attainment in the proxy and paid 105%, so a fifth of the bonus paid above target on a measure the proxy does not score. In the 2023–2025 long-term plan a three-year compensation-adjusted EPS CAGR of 0.6% earned a 128% payout on its half, which tells us the target sat below it, while the relative TSR modifier was 0% for a third-quartile ranking. Related-person transactions require Governance and Policy Committee approval under a written policy, and the excerpt records the approved employment of a related person. Two director relationships were tested for independence: a director who is an executive officer of a company that bought communications services from AT&T subsidiaries in 2025, with payments below 1% of each company's consolidated gross revenues where the NYSE standard allows up to 2%, and Mr. Kennard's under-5% interest in an investment manager whose investee transacts with AT&T; the Board judged both consistent with independence.
management.insiderOwnership: The March 2026 proxy excerpt in our pack does not include the beneficial ownership table, so we do not quantify director or executive holdings and make no claim about insider buying or selling. What the excerpt does show is the mechanism meant to substitute for ownership: at-risk target compensation for each named executive officer tied to stock price and predetermined goals, and a related-person policy with a $120,000 disclosure threshold administered by the Governance and Policy Committee.

idiosyncratic: Satellite competition. On July 2, 2026 Morningstar reported that AT&T's shares were on pace for their worst week since March 2020, and a companion headline called it a SpaceX panic. No operating metric in the quarter shows satellite taking share, and the transcript's nearest comment is that the company expects to solve many coverage corner cases for converged customers as it moves into 2027, but the episode shows the multiple reacts to satellite headlines before any churn appears. The metric to watch is postpaid phone churn relative to the 0.86% of the second quarter.

EchoStar spectrum purchase and leverage. The transaction had not closed at the time of the call, and interest expense already rose to $1,883 million in the quarter from $1,655 million a year earlier. The leverage sequence lives in the balance-sheet section; any slip in Advanced Connectivity EBITDA growth during the deleveraging window would force a choice between the buyback pace and the timetable.

Fiber ARPU and the price of convergence. Fiber ARPU fell 1.3% year over year, roughly flat excluding the acquired Lumen customers, and management expects near-term pressure as converged discounts spread; advanced home internet revenue growth of {+ +27.3% +} therefore depends on volume. If fiber net adds slow from the 367,000 of the second quarter while ARPU is still falling, segment growth would slow faster than the subscriber count suggests.

Legacy exit economics. Legacy EBITDA of $523 million in the quarter is guided to turn negative after 2027 until copper's direct costs are substantially eliminated, which depends on FCC discontinuance approvals (over 30% of wire centers so far) and on customer migration; a slower regulatory path leaves stranded cost in the income statement. Depreciation relief from fully depreciated legacy assets, which lowered second-quarter depreciation to $4,966 million from $5,251 million, is a tailwind that fades.

Benefit plans and the income statement. The February 2026 10-K notes that the company reflects annual funded-status adjustments to its pension and postretirement plans in the consolidated statement of income, so lower asset returns, higher medical costs or rate moves flow through reported earnings; the voluntary $100 million pension contribution in the quarter is a reminder that funding needs cash too.
risks.systemic: The systemic exposures are the ones the February 2026 10-K leads with, and they predate the EchoStar agreement: a higher-rate environment and inflation raising benefit costs and input prices; capital-market access, with credit-rating downgrades raising borrowing costs and potentially requiring collateral under derivative agreements, which matters more for a company carrying total debt of $144.0 billion per the release; supply-chain pressure on semiconductors and network components as hyperscaler AI spending competes for the same parts; and regulation, from FCC copper-discontinuance rulings that can speed or slow the Legacy exit to state and federal proceedings that raise operating costs. Mexico adds currency and political exposure, though it was 3.5% of FY25 revenue. Connectivity demand holds up in downturns, but the 10-K also notes that customers trade down to lower-priced plans under inflationary pressure, which is the same churn and ARPU tension that runs through this report.

body: **HOLD, target range $25–$31.** AT&T is executing: Advanced Connectivity grew service revenue {+ +5.1% +} and EBITDA {+ +8.0% +} in the second quarter of 2026, free cash flow of $4.7 billion beat the company's range, and guidance for $18 billion+ of 2026 free cash flow, a $1.11 dividend and approximately $10 billion of buybacks was reiterated. The forward multiple is undemanding, the cash yield is high, and the dividend yield of 4.18% pays investors to hold.

What stops us at HOLD is sequencing. The EchoStar spectrum purchase opens a deleveraging window during which buybacks and dividends are planned to consume all of guided free cash flow; convergence is diluting fiber ARPU; and the satellite question the risk section sets out is unresolved. Consensus already marks fair value at today's price, and our weighted value is not far above it.

We would move to BUY on the leverage ratio turning down from its post-close peak with Advanced Connectivity EBITDA growth at or above the 6%+ guided, and postpaid phone churn holding near 0.86%. We would move to SELL on churn rising, fiber net adds slowing below the second quarter's 367,000 while ARPU still falls, or a cut to the buyback to protect the timetable. Until then, the income is the return.
